content: Magnoliopsida is the botanical name assigned to a class of flowering plants. By definition, this class includes the family Magnoliaceae, but its scope can vary depending on the classification system being used. Some systems are more inclusive, while others are less so. In the Takhtajan and Cronquist systems, the term Magnoliopsida is used to refer to the group commonly known as dicotyledons. Magnoliopsida in the Takhtajan System The Takhtajan system organizes Magnoliopsida into the following subclasses: Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Nymphaeidae Subclass Nelumbonidae Subclass Ranunculidae Subclass Caryophyllidae Subclass Hamamelididae Subclass Dilleniidae Subclass Rosidae Subclass Cornidae Subclass Asteridae Subclass Lamiidae Magnoliopsida in the Cronquist System In the Cronquist system (1981 version), Magnoliopsida is divided into these subclasses: Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Hamamelidae Subclass Caryophyllidae Subclass Dilleniidae Subclass Rosidae Subclass Asteridae Magnoliopsida in the Dahlgren and Thorne Systems The Dahlgren and Thorne systems (1992) use the name Magnoliopsida to refer to all flowering plants (angiosperms). However, the Cronquist system has been widely adopted, and many versions of it have been published. In some of these Cronquist-based systems, the term Magnoliopsida, at the class level, is used to refer to all flowering plants (angiosperms). The classification includes: Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Liliidae Magnoliopsida in the Reveal System The Reveal system applies the name Magnoliopsida to a group of primitive dicotyledons, which represent approximately half of the plants within the magnoliids. The classification is as follows: Class 1: Magnoliopsida Superorder 1: Magnolianae Superorder 2: Lauranae Magnoliopsida in the APG Systems In the APG and APG II systems, botanical names are only used at the rank of order and below. For ranks above the order level, these systems use terms such as angiosperms, eudicots, monocots, and rosids, which refer to clades rather than formal taxonomic units. The class Magnoliopsida is not recognized or defined in these systems. Furthermore, the APG systems reject the idea of dicotyledons as a formal taxonomic unit, as they consider dicots to be paraphyletic.
